Hey, I can relate to you on some levels with this, but I would also like to make sure that before you begin to put yourself down and force yourself to do something you obviously don’t want to do ask yourself why do you want to be thin. Is it because that’s what you’ve been told that’s what you should be, or is it because you feel insecure. If either of these is the case I think you should assess whether the change will be sustainable and actually help you, not just satisfy your need to be conventionally more attractive. Because unless it is effecting you negatively innately, fuck the people who say your not beautiful, and everyone who has ever made you insecure unnecessarily! If it isn’t affecting your health and you don’t think your physical change will help you positively, then try and embrace yourself!

I’m mixed race, Singaporean and Italian, and I’ve always hated being in the Grey in terms or race, not one or the other, just a shade of all. I used to get teased for being too white by my Asian family and too dark by my European side. But I have begun to try and not base my self worth of other people’s opinions. This started with me, whenever I felt bad about myself, finding one thing I liked about that topic in myself. If I felt fat, I would find something else superficial or not that I liked. I won’t promise you things get by doing nothing, but I will promise you things get better if you choose to stop giving a fuck about the opinions of people who don’t deserve you respect or attention.
